content.title: Trump Wants Fannie, Freddie to Buy More Mortgage Bonds. Here’s Why.
content.summary: 0.25% or more   That's how much mortgage rates could fall if Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac buy more mortgage bonds, according to National Housing Conference Chief Executive David Dworkin.   Late Thursday, President Trump said the two government-backed companies would buy $200 billion's worth of mortgage bonds, as part of a push to make home ownership more affordable.

content.title: Trump Calls on Fannie and Freddie to Buy $200 Billion in Mortgage Bonds
content.summary: Attempting to lower housing prices, the administration is looking to step up a portfolio that was at the heart of the 2008-09 financial crisis.

content.title: Trump orders ‘my representatives’ to buy $200 billion in mortgage bonds in effort to lower housing costs
content.summary: President Donald Trump said Thursday he had ordered “my representatives” to buy $200 billion in mortgage bonds in an attempt to drive down interest rates and monthly payments, writing in a Truth Social post.

content.title: Trump says 'representatives' will buy $200B in mortgage bonds
content.description:
President Trump said in a social media post on Thursday that he is "instructing representatives" to buy $200 billion in mortgage bonds, which he says will lower monthly payments and make home ownership more affordable.

ResiClub co-founder and CEO Lance Lambert explains what this would mean for home buyers, telling Asking for a Trend host Josh Lipton that it may not make a huge dent in the housing affordability crisis.

content.title: Nvidia taps TSMC for more H200 chips due to China demand: Reuters
content.description:
Yahoo Finance Markets and Data Editor Jared Blikre tracks Wednesday's top moving stocks and biggest market stories in this Market Minute.

Mortgage rates were at their lowest level of 2025 through Tuesday, with the 30-year rate at 6.15%, according to data from Freddie Mac (FMCC).

Nvidia (NVDA) has reportedly asked Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM) to ramp up production of its H200 artificial intelligence (AI) to meet high demand, according to Reuters.

Stay up to date on the latest market action, minute-by-minute, with Yahoo Finance's Market Minute.
